facts.text: Lágymányos began as a Roman settlement, first appearing in the Claudian era before flourishing under the Flavians.
By the Severan era, the Lágymányos settlement was abandoned, marking the end of its early Roman presence.
Today, the Budapest University of Technology and Economics sits in Lágymányos, hosting several faculties of Eötvös Loránd University.
Commuters and tourists alike rely on trams 4 and 6, which run directly through Lágymányos.
After the Soviet bloc dissolved, Budapest—including Lágymányos—welcomed a wave of Western tourists amid economic transition.
Lágymányos’s name reflects its historical roots, with “Lágymányos” meaning “low hill” in Hungarian, hinting at the area’s gentle topography.
